1.why: All six screens are static cards with no animation, carousels, or modal pop-ups, though the dark Logs panel adds visual noise.

2.why: Headings and blue primary buttons are prominent, but the large dark 'Logs' panel competes for attention and the acceptance checkbox in step 4 is rendered as a tiny, misaligned control that is easy to miss.

3.why: Each screen has one field and one button so the next action is findable, yet the required MFA security code is only obtainable by scanning a developer Logs panel, which is not an obvious place to look.

4.why: The flow requires transferring a 64-character hex recovery code and a separate 6-digit code read out of a log panel, plus creating a new password, so several items and rules must be carried across steps.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, or 'remember me' option appears on any of the six screens.

6.why: Nothing saved or familiar is surfaced — no masked email, no stored account reference, no previously used identifier is displayed for recognition.

7.why: Sentences are short and plain (e.g., 'Enter the email address or account reference you normally use'), though terms like 'MFA', 'simulated delivery channel' and the long hex string are not lay-reader friendly.

8.why: No error or validation message is visible anywhere in the six screenshots, so the claim cannot be observed as true of this system.

9.why: Only the demo 'Test recovery code' is shown as a sample value; there is no example format for the email/account reference, the security code, or any password rules/examples.

10.why: Only one recovery path (emailed code) exists — no password, biometric/face, or alternative login choices are presented or explained.

11.why: Each step presents a single input and a single primary button, so the user is never confronted with multiple competing options.

12.why: Status banners ('If an eligible account exists, recovery instructions have been prepared.'), the running Logs entries, and the green 'Recovery complete' confirmation communicate the result of each action.

13.why: A persistent 'Stay safe' card and one or two explanatory sentences per step give some guidance, but these are security warnings rather than task tips, and no help link or per-field hint is offered.

14.why: No back, cancel, 'resend code', or 'start over' control appears on any screen, so recovering from a mistyped code or wrong email is not visibly supported.

15.why: Every screen reuses the same header, card layout, typography, blue primary button, 'Stay safe' block, and Logs panel in the same positions.
